title: Redis
subtitle: Redis Streams carry my execution substrate's command bus with Lua-atomic job promotion, the agent runtime's messaging, and the write-behind queue. Topology is explicit and documented.
lede: FAFO Core and Function Forge needed a backbone for job state and real-time control that could take bursts, and I put it on Redis. Each function has pending, processing and dead-letter queues and per-job state keys, and multi-step state changes run as server-side Lua, so each is atomic in one round trip. Control commands travel on a Redis stream read by a consumer group, with a separate high-priority stream so a pause or drain never waits behind bulk traffic. Container port ranges are leased with set-if-absent keys, and cloud GPU spend is counted per second in Redis and persisted to PostgreSQL. The API integration platform runs on a stock Redis 8 with append-only and snapshot persistence.
quote: I treat Redis as a component with chosen semantics.
evidence: Redis Streams and queue design: a command bus on consumer groups with a separate high-priority stream so pause and drain never wait behind bulk traffic, and job promotion as atomic Lua.
Reliable message delivery and crash recovery: agent inboxes on consumer groups that reclaim unacknowledged messages after a fence and set poison messages aside.
Data store failure-mode design: Redis instances split by role, caches that evict and a write-behind queue with eviction off that refuses work rather than drop a write.
author: Corey James
